steps.visual_purpose: A DataFrame drawn as columns side by side, each column highlighted as a Series, all sharing the same index on the left.
A small CSV file as plain text on the left and the DataFrame it becomes on the right, with the file path argument pointing at the source.
The same small orders table built two ways, from a dict of columns and from a list of row dicts, with columns and rows matching.
The outputs of head, shape, dtypes, info and describe on one DataFrame, each labelled with the question it answers.
One table shown twice, with row labels highlighted for a loc slice and positions 0 to n-1 highlighted for an iloc slice, making the stop-included versus stop-excluded difference visible.
A table with a True/False column computed beside it, and the filtered table showing only the rows marked True.
An unsorted orders table and the same table sorted by one column with a second column breaking ties, the tie groups visibly marked.
A table before and after rename, with the renamed column headers and the renamed row label highlighted and the unchanged labels visibly the same.
A column of numeric strings with its dtype beside it, and the same column after astype with a numeric dtype.
A text date column and its dtype, then the converted datetime column beside a month column pulled from it.

tiles.title: Text Cleaning, Duplicates, and Missing Data

steps.visual_purpose: A messy city column with mixed case and stray spaces, and the same column after .str.strip().str.lower() with the matching values now identical.
A table with a repeated customer ID marked, and the table after drop_duplicates with only the first occurrence of each ID remaining.
A table with blank cells highlighted, then one version with the rows dropped and another with the blanks filled, each change visible.
describe() output for a numeric column with the mean, std, median (50%) and extremes labelled, beside the matching single-method results.
A column of three-letter codes beside the column of full names produced by a dict lookup, each code matched to its label.
A DataFrame with an arrow down each column for axis=0 and an arrow across each row for axis=1, with the function's result collected at the end of each arrow.
Rows split into groups by a key, an aggregation applied inside each group, and the per-group results combined into one summary table.
A wide table with one column per month and the long table it becomes, with the identifier column staying put and the month columns turning into rows.
Three same-column tables, then one combined table with their rows stacked in order; a second view shows two tables joined side by side as extra columns.
Two small tables with a shared key column, showing which rows survive under inner, left, right and outer merges and where NA fills appear.
A long transactions table and the wide pivot table it becomes, with index values becoming rows, column values becoming headers and repeated pairs combined by aggfunc.
Two CSV outputs of the same table, one with an extra leading index column and one without it.
